answer: A stake-bonded registry works like a trellis: each agent locks a deposit that grows with its reputation, so spawning fake identities gets ruinously expensive. Honest agents climb steadily, while a Sybil tide trying to flood the network hits a canyon of cost — every fake account needs its own locked stake, and misbehavior slashes it. Deposits refund only after a clean history, so attackers pay upfront and lose it when caught.
